classification_reasons: Spec is not tight in the article's sense even after round 3: it hits sdlc.yaml risk_list item 'auth' end to end, and Flagged concern 3 accepts a residual heuristic-parsing gap (unlisted wrappers, decoded/piped content) rather than eliminating it, closed only partially in CI by the sandbox layer and not at all on native Windows.

Blast radius is wide: shell_guard.py's decide() runs on every Bash/PowerShell call in every phase, by hand and in CI; plugin/ci/settings.ci.json and plugin/ci/run_phase.py's ci_settings_file gain a new sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite rule read by every CI phase job; three pre-existing tests (test_ci.py, test_evals.py x2) have their contracts changed on purpose.

No existing test exercises a Bash/PowerShell write to a guardrail or locked test file today -- that bypass is exactly the intent's finding -- so the planned behavior is new, not already covered by current tests, even though the plan correctly orders reproducing-tests-first.
attempted: Confirmed the scope of this re-run first: compared the commit this prompt names (34a62beb3c) against the previously-reviewed commit (feed340cfc) via the commit log ('fix(0002): record the fix-response for round 3') and the git status snapshot, which shows only evidence/diff-b.patch, evidence/gate-b.json, evidence/hook-log.jsonl and status.yaml as changed since that commit (gate bookkeeping, not design content) -- spec.md and plan.md are not in that list, so the design artifacts I judge are byte-identical to the ones already reviewed under feed340cfc.

Read the new content directly rather than trusting the prompt's characterization of it: evidence/fix-response.md's round-3 entry (the only new prose in the diff) against evidence/fix-requests.json's actual round-3 review body (id 5465295155, 13 items) item by item. All 13 items are represented accurately (contract-changing test updates named and reasoned, template/.claude/settings.json and the 0006 case/workflow dropped with their stated reasons, case 0002 deferred to phase (e) with case.py's --force behavior cited, the parser declared self-contained, the sandbox block's directory-naming and _ANCHORED_RULE precedent, the scanner-literal rewrite, the route.py:468 sentence, the cd/non-literal and 2>&1/>/dev/null additions, and the plan.md Files/Order-of-work/Risks/Proof rewrites) -- no item silently dropped or misstated in the new entry.

Re-verified spec.md and plan.md in full against intent.md's Proposed outcome and against the codebase facts they cite (hooks.json's actual matcher entries for plan_sync.py, production_gate.py, panel_blind.py; protected_paths.py's GLOBAL_PROTECTED; check_test_lock's docstring; route.py:468's change_type ternary; run_phase.py:1067's _ANCHORED_RULE scope; evals/cases/0005-hooks-loaded's shape) -- unchanged from the prior review and still accurate; no drift toward a different problem than intent.md states.

Checked REVIEW.md's 'do not report' list: evidence/** is explicitly out of scope for findings, and the only substantive addition in this diff is an evidence file (fix-response.md) documenting review-response traceability, not a design or code change -- consistent with phase (b) producing no toolchain logs and no plugin/template source edits (confirmed against the diff's --stat header: all 20 changed files are under changes/0002-.../).

Proof: no test code or toolchain output exists yet (phase (b) is design-only); plan.md's Proof section still correctly lists tests as not yet written. The runner's own stale records (claude-b.json, run-b.json, gate-b.json as previously committed) are not cited for or against this verdict, per instructions -- they describe an earlier run than the one that produced this HEAD.

Blast radius and policies: re-confirmed sdlc.yaml's risk_list carries 'auth', status.yaml's risk_accepted correctly carries it with risk_accepted_by left empty (matching round 2's decision 1, the owner's by-hand acceptance route), and no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) appears in the diff. coding-standards rule 4 (no weakening) is still satisfied: the three pre-existing tests whose contracts change are each named and reasoned as deliberate, not silent, changes.

Tests: re-checked that plan.md's Order of work still puts reproducing tests first, imported inside test functions so a failure cannot abort collection, and that Acceptance/Proof describe tests that would actually exercise the Bash/PowerShell bypass rather than merely restating the design's prose -- unchanged from the prior review's finding, still sound.
